northStar.name: The Drafting Table
northStar.summary: A calm, dense, desktop-native workspace for editing, searching, navigating, reviewing, and steering agents without breaking flow.

app-bg.usage: Main app background and content surfaces in light mode.

surface.usage: Toolbars, in-pane find bars, gutters, and compact controls.

action.usage: Primary actions and high-confidence active chrome.

accent.usage: Current match, current reference, keyboard focus, and code navigation target.

danger.usage: Failed saves, destructive actions, and broken workspace state.

title.purpose: Active file titles, selected tabs, and major working-surface labels.

body.purpose: Transcript text, result labels, menu items, and compact descriptions.

label.purpose: Scope chips, counters, mode labels, and keyboard hints.

mono.purpose: Editor text, result line previews, paths when alignment matters, and command literals.

motion.rule: Motion conveys open, close, selection, loading, and route transitions only.

mustAvoid: global full-width bar for local search
different visual grammar per search type
search UI detached from transcript column

resultRows.anatomy: icon, primary label, secondary path or scope, preview, trailing count or shortcut

commandSurface.placement: top anchored sheet for global command-like actions, docked or inline for sustained work

do: Design by workflow: edit, search, navigate, review, ask agent, return.
Give every search surface a scope, result count, keyboard path, and empty or stale state.
Use one row anatomy for quick open, project search, references, diagnostics, and session search.
dont: Do not treat feature parity as UX quality.
Do not stretch a session find bar across the whole app when it searches only the chat transcript.
Do not make reference search feel like a static report.
Do not rely on right-click as the primary discovery path for editor actions.
Do not encode important state with a tiny dot alone.
